calls.head: The Lightning will send their checkers at Scheifele
calls.body: At home, the Lightning keep sending Mikheyev’s line (Mikheyev, Girgensons and Holmberg) out against opponents’ first lines, far more often than chance would suggest. Jon Cooper has been using this group as a checking line on the other team’s top line. Tonight the Jets’ first line is Connor, Scheifele and Perfetti.

calls.head: Skinner is due against the Lightning
calls.body: Skinner has been shaky against the Lightning since 2023-24, well below his usual. But three seasons of data say a goalie’s record against one team tells us nothing about the next meeting, so don’t be surprised if he looks like himself tonight.

calls.head: Who drives the play: the Lightning
calls.body: At 5-on-5, the Lightning have been one of the league’s best at getting more of the chances than they give up, and the Jets near the bottom. The ice should tilt the Lightning’s way, even if goaltending and bounces have the final say on the score.

calls.head: Picky vs. Trigger-happy
calls.body: The Lightning wait for good looks, but the Jets settle for hopeful ones. Tampa Bay is one of the league’s best for shot quality, and Winnipeg is one of the worst. The more dangerous chances should be the Lightning’s.

surprises.head: Tampa Bay’s power play was at its best
surprises.body: Tampa Bay’s power play has been near the top of the league for years. Even by those standards, this was a big night: 19.1 expected goals per 60 on the power play, against their usual 7.7 and a league average of 7.7. A team strays this far about once every 70 games.

story.head: The Lightning survive a scare
paras: This one got way too interesting for the Lightning. Neal Pionk, who scores in about 1 game in 12, scored twice. Brayden Point got the scoring started for the Lightning early in the first, but Pionk tied it up for Winnipeg late in the period, in his 600th NHL game. The second period belonged to the Lightning. Conor Geekie put the Lightning ahead for good midway through the period. Anthony Cirelli and John Carlson scored a little over two minutes apart late in the period to stretch the lead to 4-1. Brandon Hagel made it 5-1, 56 seconds later, with Cirelli picking up his 200th NHL assist on the goal, and that one stood up as the winner. It was a busy third period. Winnipeg pulled Stuart Skinner after five goals and turned to Nico Daws to start the third. Dylan Samberg and Pionk scored just under two minutes apart early in the third to cut Tampa Bay’s lead to 5-3. With the goalie pulled and less than three minutes left, Kyle Connor made it 5-4, and Pontus Holmberg shut the door with an empty-netter with a minute and a half left. Holmberg finished with four points on a goal and three assists, and Cirelli had a goal and two assists.

The Lightning carried the play, outshooting the Jets 31-21, and got the result to match. Andrei Vasilevskiy made 17 saves for the Bolts. The Lightning moved to 8-3-1 and climbed to third in the Atlantic, while the Jets dropped to 4-6-3, seventh in the Central.
